title: Gordon Ramsay's Slow-Roasted Pork Belly with Fennel
ingredients: 1 bulb fresh fennel, trimmed and roughly sliced
Olive oil, sea salt, and black pepper
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). Score the skin in a diamond pattern at 1.5 cm intervals, cutting through the fat without piercing the meat.

Place a stovetop-safe roasting tray on medium heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add sliced fresh fennel, fennel seeds, cardamom pods, star anise, garlic cloves, and bay leaves. Season lightly and fry for 2–3 minutes until fragrant.
Season the underside of the pork with salt and pepper, then place it skin-side down in the tray directly over the aromatics. Sear for 2–3 minutes until the skin begins to crisp.
Flip pork skin-side up. Pour in white wine and simmer until reduced by half. Add chicken stock until it reaches about halfway up the pork (do not submerge the skin).
Transfer the uncovered roasting tray to the oven. Slow-roast for 2 hours 30 minutes until the meat is fork-tender and the crackling is golden and blistered.
Transfer pork to a carving board to rest for 10-15 minutes.
Skim excess fat from the tray juices, stir in wholegrain mustard, reduce slightly over medium heat, and strain to create rich pan gravy.
notes: Featured in Gordon Ramsay's Ultimate Cookery Course. Keeping the skin completely dry and above the braising liquid is the secret to blistered crackling.
